_about: Registry of agent incident classes. Field detect: how the class is recognised by the machine from the event ledger (auto), from the ledger plus an open contract (auto_with_contract), or only by hand (manual). Field rationale: why the class exists, i.e. the failure mode it was seeded from. The classes were seeded from failure modes observed over weeks of real Claude Code use by one operator; they are a starting vocabulary, not a benchmark.

LOOP.name: Retry loop
LOOP.definition: The same tool call (same signature) three or more times in a row within a window of ten calls, including a repeat of a failing command, or four or more times without failures.
LOOP.rationale: Observed: dozens of rounds of edits and reruns on the wrong axis, each producing no new knowledge.
LOOP.cost_hint: turns and tokens without new knowledge

BLIND_EDIT.name: Blind edit
BLIND_EDIT.definition: An Edit of a file that was not read once in this session before the edit.
BLIND_EDIT.rationale: Observed: editing one file while another one actually runs; overwriting a parallel session's changes; edits that bypass the harness read-before-edit rule through shell appends.
BLIND_EDIT.cost_hint: overwritten changes, the wrong file edited

FLOOD.name: Context flood
FLOOD.definition: The result of a single tool call longer than 20,000 chars entered the context whole.
FLOOD.rationale: Observed: files of hundreds of KB read whole, filling most of the window and degrading later answers.
FLOOD.cost_hint: context window and cache; the model gets dumber as the window fills

STALL.name: Idle waiting
STALL.definition: More than 30 minutes passed between a tool call and its result (waiting for a permission prompt or a hung process).
STALL.rationale: Observed: a session sat for 11 hours on a permission prompt nobody answered.

TOOL_ERROR_BURST.name: Tool error burst
TOOL_ERROR_BURST.definition: Three or more erroneous tool results in a row.
TOOL_ERROR_BURST.rationale: Observed: false blocks by guard hooks made the model try workarounds instead of the task.

FANOUT.name: Subagent fan-out
FANOUT.definition: Four or more Agent calls in a single model message without a stated reason.
FANOUT.rationale: Observed: several waves of parallel subagents burned the plan limits, and subagent spend was invisible to naive cost probes.

UNVERIFIED_CLAIM.name: Done without evidence
UNVERIFIED_CLAIM.definition: Completion words in the final text of a turn (done, finished, fixed, verified, sent, pass) with zero tool calls in that turn.
UNVERIFIED_CLAIM.rationale: Observed: green reports on empty results; a 'sent' claim not backed by any outgoing log.

REPEAT_ORDER.name: Owner repeats an order
REPEAT_ORDER.definition: The owner's message repeats an instruction already given (identical normalised text or 80 % word overlap with a message from the past 14 days).
REPEAT_ORDER.rationale: Observed: a large share of one owner's messages were repeated orders, i.e. the first one was not carried out or not recorded durably.
REPEAT_ORDER.cost_hint: the owner's attention, the most expensive resource in the system

SCOPE_CREEP.name: Scope creep
SCOPE_CREEP.definition: An edit to a file outside the zone declared in the task contract.
SCOPE_CREEP.rationale: Observed: agents touching files of other work streams, overwriting others' work and making review impossible.
SCOPE_CREEP.cost_hint: someone else's work overwritten, review impossible

BUDGET_OVERRUN.name: Overrun without checkpoint
BUDGET_OVERRUN.definition: The task's spend exceeded the contract budget with no task.checkpoint event before the overrun.
BUDGET_OVERRUN.rationale: Observed: token crises caused by runs with no ceiling; a budget ceiling should end in BLOCKED, not in an endless loop.

DEAD_BARRIER.name: Barrier died silently
DEAD_BARRIER.definition: A registered hook or gauge stopped firing, and the thing that noticed was not a liveness check.
DEAD_BARRIER.rationale: Observed: most of a set of registered hooks stayed dead for weeks after a configuration edit.
DEAD_BARRIER.cost_hint: every rule the barrier was holding

RULE_WITHOUT_BARRIER.name: Rule without a barrier
RULE_WITHOUT_BARRIER.definition: A new rule is written as text with no trigger point in code.
RULE_WITHOUT_BARRIER.rationale: Observed: rules kept only as prose were broken every time.

META_INSTEAD_OF_PRODUCT.name: Meta instead of product
META_INSTEAD_OF_PRODUCT.definition: An incident was answered with a new document, gauge or rule rather than a change to the product.
META_INSTEAD_OF_PRODUCT.rationale: Observed: dozens of files of text produced per single shown artifact.

MEMORY_LOST.name: Project memory not attached
MEMORY_LOST.definition: The session was launched from a directory that has no project memory attached, and worked blind.
MEMORY_LOST.rationale: Observed: sessions started from the wrong directory redid finished work and reversed settled decisions.
MEMORY_LOST.cost_hint: redoing finished work and already cancelled decisions

MEASURING_BECAME_COST.name: Measurement became the cost
MEASURING_BECAME_COST.definition: The control instrument costs more than it saves: hook latency, injections into context, cold starts.
MEASURING_BECAME_COST.rationale: Observed: guard hooks spawning several processes per Write, and a quota guard that spent minutes per day in dead waiting.
MEASURING_BECAME_COST.cost_hint: minutes and tokens on every turn

FALSE_BLOCK.name: False barrier block
FALSE_BLOCK.definition: A barrier stopped a legitimate action; the agent spends turns on workarounds or gives up.
FALSE_BLOCK.rationale: Observed: a large fraction of blocks from one set of guards were undeniably false or left no alternative.
